public_rationale: The board fired Altman on November 17, 2023 and said he was 'not consistently candid in his communications' with it (e1). The WilmerHale review found that this public statement accurately described the board's decision and reasons (e2). It also found that the decision did not come from concerns about safety or the pace of development, but from a breakdown of trust (e3). Board member Helen Toner later said he was fired for withholding information and lying to the board (e4). Nothing in the record ties the firing to an AGI breakthrough. The claim that AGI still had not been reached is graded separately.
limitations: Only OpenAI's summary of the review is public.
The review does not mention AGI by name.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI's board fired Sam Altman in November 2023 not because AGI had been achieved (which still has not happened) but because he was not consistently candid, just as the board said.

statement.excerpt: The board fired Altman, once AI’s golden boy, in November 2023 not because AGI had been achieved (that still hasn’t happened) but because he was “not consistently candid,” just like they said.
statement.document_title: BREAKING: Sam Altman’s greed and dishonesty are finally catching up to him

from_speaker: not because AGI had been achieved
because he was 'not consistently candid,' just like they said
our_interpretation: The claim has two parts. First, the board's real reason for firing Altman was his lack of candour, as its public statement said. Second, the reason was not that AGI had been achieved.
The parenthetical 'that still hasn't happened' is graded separately in claim d386bb.
The best tests are the board's own statement, the later independent law-firm review of the board's reasons, and accounts by board members who voted to fire him.
criteria.support_condition: The board's statement gave lack of candour as the reason, and later reviews or board members confirm that this, or a loss of trust, was the real reason and that it was not an AGI breakthrough.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible evidence that the firing was mainly driven by a belief that AGI or a major capability breakthrough had been achieved, or that the stated candour reason was a pretext.

evidence.excerpt: ChatGPT-maker Open AI said Friday it has pushed out its co-founder and CEO Sam Altman after a review found he was "not consistently candid in his communications" with the board of directors.
evidence.explanation: Confirms the board fired Altman in November 2023 and gave lack of candour as the stated reason.

evidence.excerpt:
WilmerHale reviewed the public post issued by the prior Board on November 17 and concluded
that the statement accurately recounted the prior Board’s decision and rationales.
evidence.locator: Summary of WilmerHale review & findings, paragraph 4
evidence.explanation: The independent review found that the board's public statement accurately described its real reasons. This supports 'just like they said'.

evidence.excerpt:
WilmerHale also found that the prior Board’s decision did not arise out of concerns regarding
product safety or security, the pace of development, OpenAI’s finances, or its statements to
investors, customers, or business partners.
evidence.locator: Summary of WilmerHale review & findings, paragraph 4
evidence.explanation: The review rules out safety and pace-of-development concerns as the cause. An AGI breakthrough would fall under those concerns. The same passage attributes the firing to a breakdown of trust.

evidence.excerpt: Former OpenAI board member Helen Toner said that CEO Sam Altman was fired because he withheld information and lied to the board
evidence.explanation: One of the four board members who voted to fire Altman says on the record that the reason was candour and honesty with the board.
